about.title: Victorville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Victorville sits where High Desert commuter routes meet long-haul traffic, and its roads carry a mix of school runs, local errands, and drivers pushing north on Rt 395 or across town on Bear Valley Road, Amargosa Road, and Mojave Drive. Public records for 2025 list 522 injury collisions in the city, with 753 people hurt and 23 lives lost. Those figures are simply counts, but every one of them stands for a person trying to sort out what comes next. The same records show crashes clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., as the work week winds down and traffic thickens. If you were hit in Victorville, what you do in the first few days matters. Photograph the vehicles, keep every medical record, and hold off on giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney serving San Bernardino County, one who takes car accident cases on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Victorville Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: California gives most injured drivers two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but a claim involving a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle or roadway can carry a window as short as six months. The attorneys we connect you with sort out which clock applies to you before it becomes a problem.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Close the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for the crash; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and our connection service itself is free. California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, so pain and disruption to your life count, not just the bills.

items.question: My crash was on Rt 395 near Victorville. Does it matter that it may be a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If a road condition, signal, or a government-owned vehicle played a role, part of your claim may need to go through a government claims process with a deadline as short as six months, far sooner than the usual two years. An attorney can quickly check who controls that stretch of road and file the right paperwork on time. Meanwhile, save photos of the scene and any dashcam footage you have.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use small inconsistencies or offhand remarks to shift blame under California's comparative fault rules. Report the crash to your own insurer as your policy requires, but keep it factual and brief.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in California?
items.answer: For most car accident injury claims, California allows two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. Claims against a government entity follow a separate, much shorter process, sometimes just six months to submit an administrative claim. Because evidence like skid marks and nearby camera footage disappears fast, reaching out early tends to help regardless of the deadline.
